newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnlines sees clearly better 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Finnlines sees clearly better 1996 profit.

text.p: Finnish cargo shipping group Finnlines Oy said in a statement on Friday it expected its full-year 1996 profit to be clearly better than in 1995.
"Unless surprises happen in the operating environment during the end of the year, Finnlines' full-year result will be clearly better than last year," Finnlines said in its January-August report.
In 1995, group profit before extraordinary items and taxes was 315 million markka.
Finnlines reported a 49.5 percent rise in eight-month profits before extras and tax to 302 million markka.
Finnlines said export volumes were still clearly lower than in 1995, due partly to weak markets for forest industry products and partly to slow economic growth in Finland's key export markets.
"During autumn, the export outlook for the paper industry has been expected to improve slightly," the company said.
In January-July, the volume of Finnish exports through ports fell nine percent with paper exports down 14 percent. Imports through ports fell about four percent, Finnlines said.
Group net sales fell to 1.31 billion markka in January-August from 1.58 billion in the year-ago period.
Finnlines said its income statement excluded the 1996 performance of divested forwarding and logistics unit Huolintakeskus. In January-August last year, this unit's net sales were 310 million markka.
Finnlines' eight-month operating profit improved to 331 million markka from 239 million. It booked 118 million markka operating income from the divestment of Huolintakeskus.
At end-August, group liabilities totalled 1.93 billion markka, down from 2.17 billion at end-August last year.
